# How to Try an AI Video Avatar on Your Phone in Five Minutes

> **In short:** You can make a talking AI avatar from your phone's browser in about ten minutes using HeyGen's free tier — pick a face, type a short script, tap generate, and you've got a video. The interactive chat mode is also free to try, though credit limits apply.

Picture this: it's a quiet Sunday morning, you're trying to get your head around the basics of investing, and instead of reading another dry article, a friendly face on your phone walks you through it — and you can interrupt to ask follow-up questions. That's what an **AI video avatar** does. Think of it as a YouTube video you can actually have a conversation with.

Here's a beginner-friendly way to make your first one today, even if you've never touched AI video before.

## Before you start

You'll need:

- A phone with an up-to-date browser — **Chrome** on Android or **Safari** on iPhone work best
- An email address you can check right now
- About ten minutes of quiet time
- A HeyGen account on the **free tier** — no credit card needed for the first few videos

There's no app to install. Everything happens in your phone's browser. If you don't already have one, signing up takes about 30 seconds.

## Step 1 — Create your HeyGen account

Open your phone's browser and go to **heygen.com**. Look for a **"Get Started"**, **"Sign Up"**, or **"Try Free"** button — it's usually top-right or centered in the homepage banner. Tap it, enter your email, choose a password, then open the verification email HeyGen sends you and tap the link inside.

What you'll see next: a dashboard with your name in the top corner and a row of options like **Create Video**, **Avatar**, and **Recent Projects**.

💬 **Example entry:** *"[email protected]"* plus a password you'll remember.

You'll know it worked when you land on the dashboard and the "Create Video" button is visible without any "please verify your email" banner blocking it.

## Step 2 — Pick a stock avatar

Tap the option to start a new video. A grid of preset avatars appears — digital faces in different ages, styles and outfits. Tap any one to preview, then tap the small play button to see a short demo clip of that face speaking.

Don't agonise over the choice. For a first test, just pick the one whose voice and face you find least off-putting. You can change it later.

💬 **Example filter:** if you see a "Public Avatars" or "Stock" tab, stay on that one — those are free to use. Custom "Photo Avatar" uploads usually cost extra credits.

You'll know it worked when the avatar's name appears at the top of the screen and a script input area shows up below the preview.

## Step 3 — Type your script

Find the text box — it's usually labeled **Script**, **Text**, or **What to say**. Type something short. Under 150 words is ideal for a first try. Plain English is fine, and so is something you already know well, so you can judge whether the result sounds right.

💬 **Example script:** *"Hi! Here's a quick explainer on how compound interest works. Imagine you save one dollar and it earns five percent a year. After year one, you have one dollar and five cents…"*

You'll know it worked when a word count or character count shows under the text box and no red error message appears.

## Step 4 — Generate the video

Below the script, look for a button called **Generate**, **Create Video**, or **Submit**. Tap it. Rendering takes one to three minutes — leave the browser tab open and in the foreground. Closing it can cancel the job and waste your free credit.

What you'll see: a progress bar or spinner, then a play button on the finished video.

💬 **Example setting:** if you see a language dropdown, leave it on **English** unless you specifically want another language. The default voice works for most Aussie accents.

You'll know it worked when you tap play and the avatar speaks your script with lip-sync that roughly matches the words.

## Step 5 — Try the talking version

Back on the dashboard, look for an option called **Interactive Avatar**, **Streaming Avatar**, or **Avatar Chat**. This is the two-way mode — you type a question, the avatar answers on video in near real-time. It uses more credit than a normal video, so stick to one short question for this first go.

💬 **Example question to type:** *"Can you summarize what you just said in two sentences?"*

You'll know it worked when a video reply appears in the chat window within a few seconds of hitting send, and the avatar's mouth moves while it talks.

## Common mistakes

- **Mistake:** Writing a 500-word script for a first try. **Fix:** Keep your first script under 150 words. You'll spot awkward phrasing faster and you stay inside the free credit limit.
- **Mistake:** Closing the browser tab while the video is generating. **Fix:** Leave the tab open in the foreground until the play button appears. Closing early can cancel the job.
- **Mistake:** Picking the very first avatar without listening to the voice. **Fix:** Always tap the preview play button. The voice matters as much as the face — some sound warmer, some sound flat.
- **Mistake:** Expecting the interactive avatar to remember a long chat. **Fix:** Treat each question as standalone. After a few turns the avatar may lose context and start repeating itself.

## What this means for you

- **If you're learning something new:** use an avatar to explain a topic you keep forgetting. Seeing a face walk you through it often sticks better than re-reading the same paragraph.
- **If you run a small business or lead a team:** start with one question you answer over and over — a return policy, a software login fix — and make a 60-second avatar video for it. It can save you dozens of repeated replies each week.
- **If you're just curious:** spend ten minutes making an avatar that explains your own job back to you. It's the fastest way to feel both the strengths and the limits of this technology at once.

## Wrap-up

AI video avatars are no longer a tech demo — they're a free trial away, and most work fine inside a phone browser. Pick one tool, follow the steps above, and make something today, even if it's silly. Start small, notice what feels useful, and decide from there. The best way to learn what this can do for you is to actually try it once.
